subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured credential-shaped skills.entries.<skill>.env keys be allowed into skill-owned host exec subprocesses, and how should unrelated generic exec strip those secrets?
rationale: The current code violates documented host skill-env behavior for real users, but a broad fix changes credential propagation into executable child processes and overlaps active generic-exec secret-leak hardening.

options.title: Allow skill-scoped host exec env
options.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while preserving dangerous-key blocks and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

options.title: Require metadata declarations
options.body: Keep credential-shaped names blocked unless the skill declares them in metadata, then update gog metadata or ClawHub packaging and docs accordingly.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Document that credential-shaped per-skill env names are intentionally blocked and require top-level/system env or a different explicit env path.

recommendation.title: Allow skill-scoped host exec env
recommendation.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while preserving dangerous-key blocks and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses documented skills behavior, env security defaults, and credential-to-exec policy where steipete has the strongest recent history signal.
